claim: Time-ChIP can be used to quantitatively assess histone H3.3 turnover genome-wide during differentiation of mouse ESCs.
source: To gain insight into nucleosome dynamics, and to follow how dynamics change during differentiation, we used a technique called time-ChIP to quantitatively assess histone H3.3 turnover genome-wide during differentiation of mouse ESCs.
evidence: The abstract states the method used and its application to measure H3.3 turnover during ESC differentiation.

claim: High turnover can be used to identify regions involved in gene regulation without prior assumptions.
source: We found that, without prior assumptions, high turnover could be used to identify regions involved in gene regulation.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding from the study.

claim: High turnover was seen at enhancers.
source: High turnover was seen at enhancers, as observed previously, with particularly high turnover at super-enhancers.
evidence: The abstract states this observation and cites previous work.

claim: Super-enhancers show particularly high turnover compared to conventional enhancers.
source: High turnover was seen at enhancers, as observed previously, with particularly high turnover at super-enhancers.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this comparative finding.

claim: Regions associated with the repressive Polycomb-Group showed low turnover in ESCs.
source: In contrast, regions associated with the repressive Polycomb-Group showed low turnover in ESCs.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding about PcG-bound regions.

claim: Turnover correlated with DNA accessibility.
source: Turnover correlated with DNA accessibility.
evidence: The abstract states this correlation was observed.

claim: Upon differentiation, numerous changes in H3.3 turnover rates were observed, the majority of which occurred at enhancers.
source: Upon differentiation, numerous changes in H3.3 turnover rates were observed, the majority of which occurred at enhancers.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding about changes during differentiation.

claim: Active enhancers are unusually dynamic in ESCs.
source: Thus, time-ChIP measurement of histone turnover shows that active enhancers are unusually dynamic in ESCs and changes in highly dynamic nucleosomes predominate at enhancers during differentiation.
evidence: The abstract concludes with this statement based on the study's findings.

claim: Changes in highly dynamic nucleosomes predominate at enhancers during differentiation.
source: Thus, time-ChIP measurement of histone turnover shows that active enhancers are unusually dynamic in ESCs and changes in highly dynamic nucleosomes predominate at enhancers during differentiation.
evidence: The abstract concludes with this statement based on the study's findings.

claim: The nucleosome consists of a histone octamer made up of two copies each of H2A, H2B, H3 and H4, around which approximately 147 bp of DNA is wrapped.
source: The simplest repeating unit of chromatin is the nucleosome consisting of a histone octamer, made up of two copies each of H2A, H2B, H3 and H4, around which approximately 147 bp of DNA is wrapped.
evidence: This is established knowledge about nucleosome structure.

claim: Histone variants include H2A.Z, H2A.X, macroH2A, H3.3, and CENP-A.
source: These include a number of histone H2A variants such as H2A.Z, H2A.X and macroH2A and histone H3 variants such as H3.3 and CENP-A (Maze et al., 2014; Skene and Henikoff, 2013).
evidence: The text lists these variants and cites references.

claim: Nucleosomes must be disrupted in order for many processes requiring DNA access to occur.
source: As nucleosomes can act as barriers to reading the DNA sequence, they must be disrupted in order for many processes requiring DNA access to occur.
evidence: This is stated as a general principle in the introduction.

claim: Transcription and the binding of proteins to regulatory regions are known to be dependent upon increased accessibility to nucleosomal DNA.
source: Transcription and the binding of proteins to regulatory regions are known to be dependent upon increased accessibility to nucleosomal DNA.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Previous studies examining nucleosome turnover genome-wide have made use of induction of epitope-tagged histone transgenes and metabolic labeling of histone proteins.
source: Previous studies examining nucleosome turnover genome-wide have made use of two main strategies – induction of epitope-tagged histone transgenes (Kraushaar et al., 2013; Yildirim et al., 2014) and metabolic labeling of histone proteins (Deal et al., 2010).
evidence: The text describes previous methods with citations.

claim: High nucleosome turnover occurs at gene bodies, regulatory elements and replication origins in Drosophila cells.
source: Such insights include high nucleosome turnover at gene bodies, regulatory elements and replication origins in Drosophila cells (Deal et al., 2010)
evidence: This finding from previous work is cited.

source: and, in mouse cells, rapid deposition of H3.3-containing nucleosomes at enhancers and promoters associated with active histone modification marks and the histone variant H2A.Z (Kraushaar et al., 2013).
evidence: This finding from previous work is cited.

source: For example, systems based on inducible histones have a lag time after induction before histones are synthesized and incorporated into chromatin.

source: In addition, they mainly look at where newly synthesized histones are deposited rather than disruption of existing histones.

source: Metabolic labeling methods such as 'CATCH-IT', on the other hand, are not specific for particular histone variants and have limited resolution at the level of individual genes.

source: Pulse labeling with a SNAP-tag specific biotin moiety leads to covalent biotinylation of the SNAP-tagged histone pool.

source: Histone dynamics can then be determined by following the loss of biotin-labeled histones over time as nucleosomes are disrupted and replaced with nucleosomes comprised of newly synthesized unlabeled histones.
evidence: The text describes how time-ChIP measures dynamics.

evidence: This is stated with multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Time-ChIP allows labeling of existing, incorporated histones.

claim: Time-ChIP is specific for particular histone variants.
source: Time-ChIP allows labeling of existing, incorporated histones, is specific for particular histone variants and allows us to study histone dynamics in vivo.
evidence: The text describes advantages of time-ChIP.

source: Time-ChIP allows labeling of existing, incorporated histones, is specific for particular histone variants and allows us to study histone dynamics in vivo.
evidence: The text describes advantages of time-ChIP.
